i0-context.title: Load baseline context
i0-context.imperative: Load the #414 brief, §7.6.2, the diagnostic, the race_weekend quali head adapter + inference path, and the ceiling harness. Record pass when loaded.

q1.title: What concretely is the race_weekend quali head, and where does a targeted fix attach without touching production?
q1.imperative: Resolve from code. Recommended answer: the head = module driver_quali_power_from_race_weekend. Its adapter (quali_power_adapter.py) builds antisymmetric pair features from WITHIN-EVENT practice pace only (qs_expected/best/variation_adj, short_run_*); trained linear weights (gold bundle weights_quali_*) map features->mu; a BT/precision solve yields pi. The diagnostic scores -pi ordering vs DB Q. A measurement-grade targeted fix attaches at the pi layer: regenerate rw pi records via run.py backtest-latent-power-module (INFERENCE on the committed bundle, no retrain), then post-process pi behind a flag, then re-score with diagnose_quali_same_pairs.py. Confirmed: head features carry NO cross-channel pace anchor (matches the §7.6.2 signature).

q2.title: Does the diagnostic's pairwise sign-accuracy metric respond to the issue's named candidates?
q2.imperative: Critical correctness check. The metric is sign of (pi_i - pi_j) vs sign of (pos_i - pos_j), pooled over shared non-tie pairs. A pure MONOTONE recalibration of pi within an event (rescale/temper magnitude) preserves all within-event orderings -> ZERO change in sign accuracy. Therefore 'recalibrate per-context evidence weighting' moves the headline number ONLY if it changes relative ordering, which requires injecting a DIFFERENT signal (the cross-channel anchor) or re-deriving pi from reweighted features (=retrain, priced-out). Recommended answer: the only in-budget lever that can move sign-accuracy is an anchor-BLEND that mixes a new ordering signal into pi. A magnitude-only recalibration is a measured no-op and should be reported as such (it sharpens #375's case).

q3.title: What is the legitimate, non-leaky reading of an anchor-blend measurement?
q3.imperative: Guard against a trivial result. The natural anchor is best_across_fp (per-driver min-sector pace over FP1/2/3) = the SAME signal whose ceiling is 0.8061, derived from the SAME FP laps the head ingests. Blending pi' = (1-a)*z(pi) + a*z(-best_across_fp) trivially -> ceiling at a=1 (it BECOMES the ceiling). The honest, decision-relevant reading is the LOW-a regime: does anchoring the head (not replacing it) recover the bulk, and does the EASY/far-apart slice (0.687 vs 0.937) close at modest a? Recommended answer: sweep a in [0,1], report the full curve, headline the EASY-slice movement, and explicitly flag that high-a is definitionally the ceiling (not a model win). Use a rank-based anchor variant as a robustness check so the verdict is not a standardization artifact.

q4.title: Which candidates are in-budget (<=~2h compute) and which are priced-out?
q4.imperative: Budget triage. Measured: one year rw record regen ~70s; full 16-pass regen (rw+rh, 2018-2025) ~20min. IN-BUDGET: (C1) cross-channel pace-anchor blend on rw pi, a-sweep + EASY slice [primary]; (C2) rank-anchor robustness variant; (C3) the measured magnitude-recalibration no-op note (free). PRICED-OUT (report, do not burn budget): retraining the rw head with the anchor as a feature (changes weights; that IS partly #375's job and needs a gold cycle), and any full conditioned-net stand-in. Recommended answer: ship C1+C2 measured + C3 noted; price out retrain-based candidates explicitly.

q5.title: What is the apples-to-apples requirement so before/after is comparable to §7.6.2?
q5.imperative: Reuse, do not fork. Recommended answer: drive before/after through scripts/diagnose_quali_same_pairs.py's EXACT pair population and primitives (shared non-tie pairs per event; ceiling recomputed per regime; NORMAL weekends; LOSO headline 2018-2024 + OOS 2025 separate). The 'before' must reproduce §7.6.2's rw=0.6149 / ceiling 0.8061 / EASY 0.687 vs 0.937 on regenerated records (validate the regen matches the committed baseline within rounding). The 'after' substitutes pi' for pi in the SAME harness. Report overall sign-acc AND the EASY/far-apart slice per candidate per a.

q6.title: What is the #408 absorption recommendation hook?
q6.imperative: #408 = learned feature-to-gap-scale head (quali_gap_scale.py / quali_pace_gap_history.py, already on main) with ~40% headroom on its target; '#375-shaped'. It learns a per-pair gap SCALE, i.e. a learned magnitude/weighting. Recommended answer: tie the absorption verdict to the C1/C3 result. If sign-accuracy needs a new ORDERING signal (anchor) rather than a better magnitude, then #408 (a scale head) addresses calibration/magnitude, not the sign-accuracy gap -> it folds into #375 as the magnitude/uncertainty component, NOT as a standalone targeted sign-accuracy fix. Confirm the direction from the C-results before writing the line.

q7.title: Protected intent + output/PR/comment mechanics (no production wiring).
q7.imperative: Pre-ruled by the brief; record as protected intent. (a) Measurement-grade only: flags/scripts, NO production default changes; do NOT touch fusion.py, fusion_training/, fusion_rework_findings.md. (b) Findings: new subsection right after §7.6.2 in docs/evo/prediction_ceiling_and_priorities.md (sole writer this wave). (c) Verdict ends with TARGETED FIX | FULL NET | BOTH-STAGED + #408 absorption line. (d) Honest negative is a complete deliverable. (e) Branch constellation/issue-414-quali-head-scoping; PR body plain-English-first + 'Closes #414'; do NOT merge/close; post verdict on #375, cross-link from #414. (f) DB-only, py, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8.

consolidation.verdict: RESOLVED: scope a measurement-grade targeted fix to the race_weekend quali head at the pi layer; primary candidate = cross-channel pace-anchor blend (a-sweep + EASY slice) measured before/after via diagnose_quali_same_pairs.py; magnitude-only recalibration is a provable sign-accuracy no-op (key finding); retrain candidates priced-out; honest negative acceptable; deliver verdict TARGETED FIX|FULL NET|BOTH-STAGED + #408 absorption line into a new subsection after 7.6.2.
